sources.title: Israel's Embassy announces the Colombian tourist visa exemption and ETA-IL
sources.publisher: Embassy of Israel in Colombia / Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual bilateral exemption announcement read. The Israeli mission names 1 September 2026, expressly requires ETA-IL for Colombians travelling to Israel, and links the PIBA application.
sources.supportingExcerpt: a measure that will come into effect as of September 1, 2026.

sources.title: Current embassy confirmation of ETA-IL for Colombian travellers
sources.publisher: Embassy of Israel in Colombia / Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual mission consular service page read. Its current introductory notice expressly says that Colombians need no visa but must complete the ETA-IL form.

sources.title: Israeli embassy guide to obtaining ETA-IL approval
sources.publisher: Embassy of Israel in Colombia / Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual embassy application guide read. It directs visa-exempt applicants to the Population and Immigration Authority form, states the qualified 90-day visitor ceiling, and distinguishes that stay from the authorization's longer validity. Older pilot-fee wording is not used.
sources.supportingExcerpt: stay for up to 90 days or less upon receipt of approval to enter

sources.title: Colombian Foreign Ministry confirms ordinary-passport tourism and the bilateral stay limit
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Colombia
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual 11 September announcement read. It states the ordinary-tourist scope and describes the Colombian traveller limit as at most 90 days within 12 months, subject to each country's procedures. Israel's explicit ETA-IL guidance governs that local procedure.
sources.supportingExcerpt: por un periodo no superior a 90 días dentro de un lapso de 12 meses

policies.title: Colombian ordinary tourists: visa exemption with ETA-IL
policies.summary: Israel restored the tourist visa exemption for Colombian ordinary passport holders from 1 September 2026. They must obtain ETA-IL approval before travel; this is a travel authorization, not a visa.
conditions: This is the ordinary-passport tourism baseline. Work, residence, special documents and other immigration categories are separate.

The Israeli embassy continues to require ETA-IL even though no tourist visa is needed. The authorization's validity is separate from how long a visitor may stay; admission and the period granted remain subject to immigration control.

allowedStays.label: Up to 90 days within 12 months, subject to admission
notes: Colombia's ministry describes this time window for Colombian travellers. Follow the stay granted by Israeli immigration; the ETA itself is not a stay permit.

application.label: Apply through the official ETA-IL service
steps: Use the Population and Immigration Authority form linked by the Israeli Embassy and enter the details of the ordinary Colombian passport you will travel with.
Submit the ETA-IL application and obtain approval before travel.
Travel with the same passport and retain the authorization for inspection. The border authority decides admission and length of stay.

conflicts.explanation: Israel restored the ordinary tourist waiver but still requires ETA-IL. The earlier bundled visa category is superseded, and the live imported visa-free category does not capture the mandatory authorization.
